summary: Almost everyone entering Tuvalu gets a visa on arrival at Funafuti for up to one month — free for citizens of the countries listed in its Immigration Regulations, among them the UK, Fiji and Samoa, AUD 100 for others — while EU passport holders (except Irish) are visa-exempt for 90 days in any 180 under the EU–Tuvalu agreement.

notes: The UK and Canada say there are no ATMs in Tuvalu and that card payments are not accepted; the UK says to bring enough Australian dollars in cash for your trip.
The UK says it is illegal to import, export, cultivate or distribute drugs in Tuvalu, with penalties that include fines and imprisonment.

payments.text: The UK and Canada both say there are no ATMs in Tuvalu and that credit and debit card payments are not accepted. The UK says to bring enough Australian dollars in cash for the duration of your trip.

safety.text: Canada's travel advice says the crime rate is very low, though petty crime occurs. The UK government's travel advice says Tuvalu's only hospital is on Funafuti and is adequate for routine treatment, that serious cases may need medical evacuation to Fiji or Australia, and that the tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to May, though cyclones can happen at any time of year.

tips.text: There are no ATMs in Tuvalu and card payments are not accepted, according to the UK and Canada. The UK says to bring enough Australian dollars in cash for the duration of your trip.
The UK advises drinking or using only boiled or bottled water and avoiding ice in drinks. Canada says shortages of fresh water occur and that bottled water may be in short supply.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Tuvalu?
faq.answer: Practically everyone can get an entry permit on arrival at Funafuti for a stay of up to one month. Citizens of the countries listed in Schedule 1 of the Immigration Regulations 2014 — including the UK, Malaysia, South Korea, Fiji, Kenya and several Caribbean states — pay nothing, other nationalities pay AUD 100 unless the Minister waives it, and EU passport holders (except Irish) are visa-exempt for 90 days in any 180 under the EU–Tuvalu agreement.

faq.question: How much does the Tuvalu visa on arrival cost?
faq.answer: AUD 100, set by the Immigration Regulations 2014, unless you are a citizen of one of the countries listed in Schedule 1 — among them the UK, Fiji, Kiribati, Samoa, Tonga, Malaysia and South Korea — who pay nothing; the Minister may also waive it. The UK Foreign Office says card payments are not accepted in Tuvalu and to bring enough Australian dollars in cash for the trip.

faq.question: Can I stay longer than a month?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK Foreign Office says that to stay longer than one month you must get an extension from the Department of Immigration in Funafuti. Under the Immigration Regulations 2014, the Principal Immigration Officer may extend a visitor permit for up to 30 days, for a fee of AUD 100, or AUD 200 if you intend to engage in business or employment.

faq.question: Are there ATMs or card payments in Tuvalu?
faq.answer: No. The UK and Canada both say there are no ATMs in Tuvalu and that credit and debit card payments are not accepted. The UK says to bring enough Australian dollars in cash for the duration of your trip.
